stem: Priya invests $\$5600$ at a rate of $2.5\%$ per year compound interest.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Calculate the interest earned during the second year.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Priya says that the total interest earned in the first 8 years will be $\$1120$. Explain why the total interest will be more than $\$1120$.
parts.answer: $\$1120 = 5600 \times \frac{2.5}{100} \times 8$ is SIMPLE interest, calculated on $\$5600$ every year. With compound interest each year's interest is calculated on the growing amount, so from the second year onwards the yearly interest is more than $\$140$ (the second year alone earns $\$143.50$), and the total is more than $\$1120$.

solution:
(a) Amount at the end of the first year $= 5600 \times 1.025 = \$5740$.
Interest earned during the second year $= 5740 \times \frac{2.5}{100} = \$143.50$.
(Alternatively: $5600 \times 1.025^2 - 5600 \times 1.025 = 5883.50 - 5740 = \$143.50$.)

(b) $5600 \times \frac{2.5}{100} \times 8 = \$1120$ is the interest if it were SIMPLE interest, calculated on the original $\$5600$ in every one of the 8 years.
With compound interest each year's interest is calculated on the growing amount, so the interest in every year after the first is more than $\$140$ (the second year earns $\$143.50$ from part (a)). Hence the total interest is more than $\$1120$.
(For reference, the actual total is $5600 \times 1.025^8 - 5600 \approx \$1223.06$.)
syllabus_check: 4052 Financial mathematics: compound interest, the interest of a given year, and the distinction between simple and compound interest. 2 marks for a two-step routine (grow one year to $\$5740$, then take $2.5\%$ of it); 1 mark for one sentence that names the error (\$1120 is the simple-interest figure) with a number in it. Every money value is exact to the cent: $5600 \times 1.025 = 5740$ and $5740 \times 0.025 = 143.50$, so no rounding is needed.
originality_note: The exemplars recover a principal from total interest, find r, find a total after simple interest, or explain a monthly-versus-yearly rate. This question asks for the interest of ONE later year (the second) — a skill none of the exemplars test — and its explain-why targets the simple-versus-compound confusion over 8 years, with fresh figures ($\$5600$, $2.5\%$) chosen so that every answer lands on exact cents. Distinct from Q3's hire-purchase context.
